trigger_or_context: Early on, you notice something that worries you.
short_term_function: Ignoring the warning lets you keep dating the person instead of stopping.
developmental_cost: You end up choosing with less real proof.
adaptive_alternative_1: When something worries you, name what you saw. Then watch it or ask about it before you get more serious.
what_new_response_supports: You learn if the worry is a one-time thing or a real pattern.
expected_discomfort_or_cost: You may sit with the chance a hopeful match won't work out.
context_conditions: If a warning is about your safety, get safe — don't test it.

trigger_or_context: You feel drawn to people who are hard to reach.
developmental_cost: You keep landing in the same spot, so you learn little about who fits you.
adaptive_alternative_1: Notice how much the other person shows up for you — texts back, keeps plans, treats you well. Give more only as they show more.
what_new_response_supports: You find out if they can really meet you back, or not.
expected_discomfort_or_cost: Someone steady may feel less exciting at first.
context_conditions: You still get to feel drawn to someone; this is about pacing, not forcing.

trigger_or_context: The other person isn't showing up, and you push harder.
short_term_function: Chasing keeps the connection going from your side even when they don't answer.
developmental_cost: You give a lot before you know they'll give back.
adaptive_alternative_1: Reach out when you want to. Then leave space to see if they reach back before you do more.
what_new_response_supports: You see if they show up too, or not.
expected_discomfort_or_cost: No answer can be an answer, and that's hard to sit with.

trigger_or_context: You get a gut feeling that something is off.
short_term_function: Ignoring the feeling means you don't have to act on it or bring it up.
developmental_cost: You stop trusting your own read, which is the heart of this pattern.
adaptive_alternative_1: Treat the feeling as a clue. Name what set it off, sort facts from your story, then watch or ask.
what_new_response_supports: You start trusting your read again, based on facts.
expected_discomfort_or_cost: You might be wrong, and you have to sit with the feeling.
context_conditions: A gut feeling is a clue to check, not a rule to obey.

trigger_or_context: You already saw clear warning signs.
short_term_function: Staying let you keep the relationship instead of ending it over the worry.
developmental_cost: You act against what you already knew, so your judgment counts for less.
adaptive_alternative_1: When you notice a real worry, use it to check and decide — not to push past it.
what_new_response_supports: You find out if the worry is a dealbreaker or not.
expected_discomfort_or_cost: You may have to make a hard choice.

trigger_or_context: The relationship isn't working, and you keep staying.
developmental_cost: You wait so long that your choice comes late.
adaptive_alternative_1: Pick ahead of time what you need to see, and by when. Then look at what really happened and act on it.
what_new_response_supports: You see if things are truly changing or just hoped for.
expected_discomfort_or_cost: You may face a hard choice or a loss.
context_conditions: Staying is fine if real change is happening; not if it's only hope.

trigger_or_context: You meet someone kind, and you brush them off.
developmental_cost: You may pass on good matches before you really check them.
adaptive_alternative_1: If you notice you're brushing off someone kind, ask if it's 'no real spark' or just unfamiliar. Give it a little more time before you decide.
what_new_response_supports: You see if real interest can grow.
expected_discomfort_or_cost: Less spark at the start, and some not-knowing.
context_conditions: Real attraction still matters — this isn't about dating people you don't like.

trigger_or_context: Someone lets you down, and you give another chance.
short_term_function: Another chance keeps the relationship going for now.
developmental_cost: Open-ended chances put off your choice.
adaptive_alternative_1: If you give another chance, name one real change you need to see, and by when. Then look at what happened.
what_new_response_supports: You see if the change is real or just hoped for.
expected_discomfort_or_cost: Holding a limit is hard, and it might end.
context_conditions: Fixing things and just waiting are not the same — this depends on whether they own their part.

trigger_or_context: You look back and see a pattern of bad matches.
review_reason: outcome-level; no discrete behavior to change

trigger_or_context: You look back and see the same relationship again and again.
The other person made promises, and you watch what they do.
short_term_function: Watching lets you see if their actions match their words.
context_conditions: This helps unless it turns into constant checking.
